# GameLogicTests/KnownAnswers.txt
#
# The twins' known answers (D20, ADR-008 item 8). A twin (GameLogicTests/TwinRig.h) plays a scenario on the interpreted
# original and on the native code, and compares the game-state digest of the two at every digest step and at the end of
# every Play. Each of those digests is recorded here from the original, so that the native code still has something to
# meet once D7 has deleted the interpreter.
#
# Format: one answer per line, three fields separated by single spaces:
#
#   TWIN ORDINAL DIGEST
#
#   TWIN     the name the twin is made with, TwinRig rig("TwinTitle")
#   ORDINAL  the digest's place in the twin, from 1, counted over all of its Play calls in order: in each Play its
#            digest steps in order, then the state the Play ends in. A twin that starts at the title screen plays
#            "wait 3" when it is made, so its answer 1 is the state that leaves.
#   DIGEST   Elite::GameStateDigest, the SHA-256 of the game's state (ADR-008 item 5), in lowercase hex
#
# Lines are sorted by twin and ordinal. Blank lines and lines that start with '#' are ignored; the recorder keeps the
# ones before the first answer, this header, and writes every answer after them, so a comment among the answers is lost.
#
# Checking: a TwinRig asserts that each digest of the original is the answer recorded for it, then that the native one
# is the original's. A NativeTwin, the form every twin takes after D7, asserts that each native digest is the answer. A
# missing answer fails the twin, naming it and the ordinal.
#
# Recording: run the tests with OUTPOST_ELITE_RECORD_KNOWN_ANSWERS=1 in one process (the test binary or vstest.console.exe
# directly, not Build/RunTests.py's parallel shards, which would write this file at once). Each twin then records the
# original's digests instead of checking them, still asserts that the native ones agree, and, if it passes, replaces its
# answers here when it is done; a twin that fails leaves its answers as they were. It is never set in CI, where it fails
# the twins. Like a replay's digests (ADR-008 item 7), an answer changes only by a ruling recorded with its cause, and
# recording is how a new twin's answers are added, never how a failing twin is made to pass.
